methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $5.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 20.5x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Rapidus is a late-stage frontier semiconductor company founded by Atsuyoshi Koike and Tetsuro Higashi. The company has raised $5B+ to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers such as Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method here. Using total capital raised of $5.0B as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $6.0B. Peer-median triangulation is not supportable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow semiconductor cohort—while 12 same-sector peers exist, none meet the minimum threshold of three datapoints in tightly filtered categories. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be applied because Rapidus does not disclose revenue, which is standard for private companies at this stage.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $5.1B to $6.9B, with a median point of $6.0B. This reflects limited methodological overlap—only one primary method is quantitatively defensible. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue visibility needed for relative valuation, the scarcity of true peer comparables at identical stage and scale, and reliance on stage-progression mechanics that assume typical funding dynamics. Additional data on operating metrics or capital deployment trajectory would tighten confidence.
